zinbTruitt

zinbTruitt fits count-data regression models without any general-purpose optimizer (optim() and friends are never called):

  • nbreg(): negative binomial (NB2) regression, using IRLS (Fisher scoring) for the coefficients alternated with Newton-Raphson for the dispersion theta. Comparable to MASS::glm.nb().
  • zinbreg(): zero-inflated negative binomial regression, using an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits. Standard errors come from the observed information matrix. Comparable to pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Developed for the STA 651 Final Project (Fall 2026), Miami University.

Website and report: https://JosephTruitt.github.io/zinbTruitt/

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("JosephTruitt/zinbTruitt")

Usage 

library(zinbTruitt)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)

# Zero-inflated negative binomial: count covariates | zero covariates
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)

AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)
predict(fit_zinb, type = "response")   # also "count" and "zero"

Methods provided

Both nbreg and zinbreg objects support print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik, fitted, residuals (response and Pearson), nobs, and predict (with newdata).

Agreement with the reference implementations

nbreg() reproduces MASS::glm.nb() and zinbreg() reproduces pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin") on pscl::bioChemists and AER::NMES1988, well inside the required tolerances (coefficients and standard errors to about 1e-8 for NB and 1e-4 for ZINB). The benchmark and simulation scripts are in inst/benchmark/ with saved results in inst/benchmark/results/.

Report

The full report (methods, benchmarking, simulation study and the NMES1988 analysis) is a Quarto document, vignettes/articles/report.qmd. It is rendered to report/report.pdf and appears as an article on the package website.

R CMD check notes

(To be updated after the final devtools::check() on the submission machine.)

No general-purpose optimizers

No function in R/ calls optim(), optimize(), nlm(), nlminb(), uniroot(), glm(), lm() or any other prohibited function. numDeriv is used only in the tests to verify the analytic Hessian.
